title: I’m loving Open AI Astra- Couldn’t sleep last night, so I vibe coded a game about my dog in Galway! Would love feedback!
author: _WhoisMrBilly_
selftext:
I used to love the Japanese import PlayStation game vibe ribbon, so I had a brainwave last night when I couldn’t sleep. I would love to do a version of that that takes music dynamically and shapes the gameplay around it. I chose roughly the same art style, but also wanted it to be about my little dog walking around our hometown in Galway.

Will include workflow down below.

comments.author: _WhoisMrBilly_
comments.body:
My workflow was basically a lot of small iterations with ChatGPT/Codex, testing mainly on my iPhone:

**Start with an idea:** a rhythm game inspired by Vib-Ribbon, starring my dog Ciara on a walk through Galway.

**Develop the art:** I supplied photos of Ciara and my house, then refined generated character images before putting them into the game. Getting her likeness and walking animation right took quite a few attempts.

**Build and test:** Codex handled the HTML/JavaScript, canvas animation and browser audio. I played each version and sent back screenshots, recordings and fairly nontechnical feedback.

**Refine the music response:** we moved beyond regularly spaced obstacles toward detecting musical accents. For one track, I recorded myself tapping where things felt natural and used that to guide a custom course.

**Add personality and polish:** Galway landmarks, rain, her yellow coat, seagulls, her penguin toy—and fixes for phone layout, audio loading and difficulty.

We also rolled back changes when they made things worse. It’s still a work in progress, especially the automatic music timing. My role has mostly been art direction, playtesting and asking “why does that look weird?”

replies.author: orellanaed
replies.body: You should try building on desktop with Godot! Using a harness like Flockbay via MCP. You'll get better results of games than browser-based games. Its a real game engine after all

replies.author: _WhoisMrBilly_
replies.body: Oh really, I haven’t used any of those. Do you have like a suggested workflow. It’s just a simple browser-based game. Do you think it really needs more than that? I’m completely open to guidance

replies.author: orellanaed
replies.body: Fair , no if its a simple game keep it browser based, but honestly I started the same way and I found real games to be much more fun to build. Either way the best choice is whatever you enjoy doing most tbh
